title: Research Progress and Trends of Deep Learning in Stock Price Prediction: A Systematic Review from LSTM to Transformer
tldr: Systematically reviews deep learning methods for stock price prediction from LSTM to Transformer, comparing ARIMA, GARCH, SVM, LSTM, and Transformer models on data requirements, indicators, and performance.
problem_and_motivation: Stock price prediction is challenged by high volatility, non-linearity, and non-stationarity. Traditional methods (ARIMA, GARCH) capture linear patterns but fail on nonlinear financial data. Deep learning offers improved accuracy but faces data noise and overfitting issues.
approach: Systematically reviews the evolution from traditional statistical models (ARIMA, GARCH) to ML (SVM, Random Forest) to deep learning (LSTM, Transformer).
Compares LSTM and Transformer architectures for sequential financial data modeling.
Analyzes data sets, evaluation metrics, and empirical performance across studies.
Discusses challenges including data noise, overfitting, interpretability, and computational efficiency.
Identifies future directions: multimodal information fusion, explainable AI, and real-time adaptive learning.
findings: LSTM excels at capturing long-term dependencies in sequential stock price data.
Transformer models offer parallel computation advantages over sequential LSTM processing.
Data noise and non-stationarity remain significant challenges for all models.
Multimodal data fusion (text, news, social media) with price data improves prediction.
Explainable AI is needed to address the black-box nature of deep learning stock models.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: Provides a systematic technical roadmap from traditional to deep learning methods for stock price prediction. Highlights the progression from ARIMA/GARCH through SVM/Random Forest to LSTM and Transformer architectures. Identifies key remaining challenges and promising research directions in the field.
directly_justifies: LSTM captures long-term dependencies in sequential price data.
Transformers offer parallel computation advantages over LSTMs.
limits: Review paper without original empirical experiments.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematically scanned all topic domains (1.A-14.C). Assigned 6.A and 6.B high relevance for predictive modeling and forecasting algorithms. Rejected behavioral, system design, and evaluation topics as the paper focuses purely on forecasting methodology.

limitations: Review paper without original experimental validation.
Limited coverage of ensemble and hybrid deep learning approaches. [unacknowledged]

LSTM captures long-term dependencies; Transformers enable parallel processing.
